subject: source directory
fact: Clone repositories into ~/source on macOS and Linux, or %USERPROFILE%\source on Windows. Create that directory if it is missing.
reason: The user keeps project checkouts in a source directory and expects a fresh machine to use it.

citations.text: User input: assume the repo hasn't been cloned yet, and that I like ~/source or <profile>\source

subject: Copilot kit bootstrap
fact: The copilot-kit repo is the bootstrap source. After setup, skills, agents, and instructions live in ~/.copilot (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\.copilot), not in each client repo.
reason: The user wants one machine-level Copilot setup instead of copying the kit into every repository.

citations.text: User input: after the bootstrapping then it should live in ~/.copilot or wherever is common on whatever platform we're using.

subject: bootstrap prompt
fact: On a new machine, clone copilot-kit into ~/source/copilot-kit (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\source\copilot-kit) and follow the bootstrap-machine skill. Do not assume the repo is already cloned.
reason: The user starts setup by pasting a short prompt into Copilot on a machine that does not have the kit yet.

citations.text: User input: I go into a new machine and open copilot, I paste a simple prompt - something like "Go to this repo and setup this machine how I like it"

subject: dev tools
fact: Keep Git, GitHub CLI, Azure CLI, the latest stable .NET SDK, PowerShell 7, Bicep, Node.js, Terraform, and AWS CLI installed, and upgrade them to latest. Use Homebrew on macOS and winget on Windows. Do not run gh auth login or az login during bootstrap.
reason: The user asked machine setup to install and upgrade these tools without interactive cloud sign-in.

citations.text: User input: checking for the latest version of dotnet and anything else that might need to be installed - azure CLI, github CLI, etc.
